description: Opt in to API-key providers (paid tokens). Absent or false: subscription-only, and no API provider is constructed.

This Foundry's own conversation settings: `joining`, the conversation permissions and outbound setting someone joining its threads starts with, per audience (built in: in your orgs every permission but `agent.act`; outside `member.log`, `member.wake`, `member.take` and `member.agent`; outbound `review` for both). A project's floor, conch and the rest are `projects.<id>.conversations`.
Global and scope schedules (Forge Master, Feedback): work this Foundry starts on its own, each run a thread. A project's are `projects.<id>.scheduler`. Local only: never in a repository.
Subscription-mode overrides; every field has a default. See docs/subscription-decisions.md.
Structural tool rules: the only tool denials, held in every permission mode (turns/tool-gate.ts).
Credential references only; do not put tokens in settings. Several of one runtime are a pool.

How a runtime with several logins balances them (Aron, 2026-11-02: "a balancing toggle… like a scale"): `routing` (default `quartile-balanced`; `pinned` is balancing off) and the login `owner-first` or `pinned` prefers. A project's `subscriptionPools` overrides it.
Kingdom subscription pools this Foundry draws main-thread logins from: one per owner's Signet (URL, credential file, pool selection).
Dev mode (R-2026-11-25-05): the `__` settings below take effect only while it is on. Anyone may turn it on. Machine only: never in a repository.

Dev mode's local Chorus host: while dev mode is on, every chorus-on project's Warden calls go to it directly, no Kingdom. `tokenKey` names the keychain entry holding its bearer token (default `CHORUS_DEV_TOKEN`); the token itself never goes in settings.
The host's base URL (http or https), e.g. `http://localhost:4900`.
The keychain entry (or environment variable) holding its bearer token, default `CHORUS_DEV_TOKEN`; Chorus's starts `CHORUS_`. Never the token.
Dev mode's local Oracle host: only its health is checked, from the Dev settings section.
The host's base URL (http or https), e.g. `http://localhost:4900`.
The keychain entry (or environment variable) holding its bearer token, default `CHORUS_DEV_TOKEN`; Chorus's starts `CHORUS_`. Never the token.
Project-scoped integration grants. Independent of inference resource selection. Restart to apply.
Which Kingdom owner's pool (and spread or selection) a given thread draws its login from, by thread id.
Explicit thread-to-source UUID assignments, applied on Foundry startup.
Background domain review phase; does not override decision or executor profiles.
The feedback lifecycle: capture, tuning prompts and the role-file changes they apply (docs/FEEDBACK-LOOP.md).
`$$word` secrets lifted into the thread's scratch pad, and paths no agent reads (FEAT-005). On by default.
The local journal (docs/THREAD-TREE.md spec A).
Days a middleware call's raw rows (its full input) stay in the journal after its turn is reduced; Archive only ever gets the reduced entries. Default 30.
How often the Wardens' guard fires: `per-turn` (default), once over a turn's whole tool activity when the turn's tool activity ends; or `per-call`, on each tool call (Aron, 2026-10-15).

What a thread becomes when its branch merges (Aron, 2026-11-01): `done` (default; the thread shows done and can take another task) or `auto-archive` (archived, its worktree released per FEAT-003). A project's `threadOnMerge` overrides it.

When you send while a thread's turn runs (CORE-001, Aron 2026-11-01): `true` (default) steers the message into that turn; `false` queues it after. A queued message can always be steered in with "Steer now". A project's `steer` (yours, then the repository's) overrides it.

Whether agents should explain non-trivial plans and loops with an interactive Blueprint diagram (`foundry:blueprint`, `set_artifact` `kind: 'blueprint'` or fenced ```` ```blueprint ```` block, R-2026-11-23-07). Default `false`. A project's `blueprintDiagrams` (yours, then the repository's) overrides it.
Where the viewer's left rail goes once you start a thread from the Projects rail (Aron, 2026-11-14): `attention` (default) returns to the Attention list, `stay` keeps Projects.
The composition view: one ladder (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, auto memory, role files) composes the instructions and domain knowledge of every role; see docs/usage-and-context.md.
Global defaults: executor provider/model + decision provider/model.
The provider new threads run on (e.g. `claude-code`, `codex`).
The model new threads run on.
Which local login (a native authentication source) threads use by default.
Which Kingdom owner's subscription pool threads use by default.
Reasoning effort for Codex threads; omitted, Codex's own default.
The decision roles' provider (Wardens, feedback routing); omitted, the decision default.
The decision roles' model; omitted, the decision default.
Vendors (keyed by vendor id: anthropic, openai, google, ...), each with an on/off switch and its subscription and API modes (models/vendors.ts).
This Foundry's installation name: what Kingdom pairing names it. Default "Foundry on <host>".
This machine's icon where machines are shown (Watchtower actors, Watching): a glyph and a slot of the theme's categorical palette (`--layer-0` to `--layer-11`).
The icon's shape (anvil, bolt, leaf, moon, peak, wave, star, hex).
The icon's colour: a slot of the theme's categorical palette, 0 to 11.
The message box: one box with a destination label (Thread · /btw · /aside), or a box per open view.
Show a message box per open view (Thread, /btw, /aside) instead of one box with a destination label.
Personal viewer customization: color scheme, custom theme, opt-in local extensions, per-slot layout, cross-pane tab placement, and component display flags. Local only.
Viewer color scheme: `dark` (default), `light`, or `system` (follow OS preference).
Named custom theme slug under `<configDir>/ui/themes/<slug>.css`, or null to use default `theme.css`.
Explicit opt-in list of local extension ids under `<configDir>/ui/extensions/` to load in the viewer.
Per-slot layout overrides (`order`, `hidden`, `pinned`) keyed by slot id.
Item ids in preferred order; unlisted new built-ins still appear after these.
Item ids hidden from this slot.
Item ids pinned at the start of this slot.

Cross-pane tab placement overrides keyed by registered side-panel tab id (`'left'` or `'right'`). Moving a registered side-panel tab ID to `'left'` or `'right'` keeps it receiving upstream component updates on whichever side it sits on.
Per-component display and behavior toggles, keyed by component id then flag name.
Global agent templates (keyed by agent ID). Projects inherit these by id; a project override of the same id wins. A fresh install is seeded from defaultAgents(): one executor.
The agent's id: its key in `agents`, and how projects extend or override it.
What the agent does in a turn: `executor`, or `warden` for a generated Warden.
Domain this agent operates in (e.g., "docs", "security", "cross-thread").

Human-readable description of this agent's role and responsibilities. File path relative to project root (e.g., ".foundry/agents/executor.md"). Explains: what this agent does, which layers it reads/writes, who it delegates to, why.
System prompt for this agent. Empty for an executor: a main thread's instructions come from its thread role.
LLM settings: provider/model default to global if omitted.
The model this agent runs on; omitted, the global default model.
Temperature, set per agent. Decisions want 0, creative agents want higher.
Warden: source ids its domain knowledge composes from, before the composition view's files (docs/usage-and-context.md, "Composition view"). A project extension appends its own.
Tool names that trigger this configured Warden's post-action guard. [] disables guards.
Whether this agent can use tools (true) or is text-only (false). Default: true.
Extended thinking / reasoning effort. "none" | "low" | "medium" | "high" | number (budget tokens).
Permission level for code execution runtimes. Default: "bypass".
Browser-specific config.
Browser interaction mode.
Whether to share authenticated browser sessions across agents.
Allowed URL patterns (glob). Empty = allow all.
Blocked URL patterns (glob). Takes precedence over allowedUrls.
Whether to capture screenshots for context.
Max page loads per dispatch (prevent runaway navigation).
Per-call timeout in ms.
Enable prompt caching for this agent.
Whether this agent is active.
When this agent runs in the pipeline: - "always": runs on every request - "on-demand": available but only invoked when middleware explicitly requests it
Global layer templates (keyed by layer ID). Projects inherit these by id; a project override of the same id wins. A fresh install has none: a thread is unwrapped until one is configured.
The layer's id: its key in `layers`, and how projects and agents refer to it.
The domain this layer holds knowledge for. A Warden owns no configured layer: its knowledge comes from its region.

Human-readable description of this layer's job in the system. File path relative to project root (e.g., ".foundry/layers/conventions.md"). Explains: what knowledge domain it covers, when it's relevant, who writes to it, what the warmed content looks like.
Instruction prompt for this layer.

Semantic segment of the layer's CONTENT in the reading view. Optional: a configured layer without it keeps the legacy id-based classification. Only "domain-knowledge" (configured/published cache) or "thread-knowledge" (generated, thread-private) are accepted; the prompt is always an instruction.
Data source IDs that feed this layer.
Staleness threshold in ms (0 = never stale).
Agent IDs that can write to this layer. Undefined = any agent.
Whether this layer definition is enabled.
When instances of this layer are included in context assembly: - "always": included on every request - "on-demand": only included when middleware explicitly requests it
Global data source templates (keyed by source ID). On a fresh install this is empty: sources are project-scoped.
The source's id: its key in `sources`, and how layers name it in `sourceIds`.
Where the content comes from: a file, database, URL, markdown, inline text, the Archive, or instruction files.

Instruction sources only (`uri` is unused): which slot of the thread's role composition the source returns. Default "instructions". Who it is for is the thread role's audience, else `composition.roles["thread:main"].audience`.
Searches the local Archive for this project; `uri` is unused.
The Archive project whose captured sessions are searched.
Most tokens of matching session text taken per search (128 to 16,000; default 2,048).
The source's display name in Settings and the layer view.
Connection string, file path or URL, depending on type.
Whether this source is enabled.

Memory-backed ("file") sources only. Widest visibility this source exposes to a thread: "thread" (default) = the thread's own captures plus project/global publications; "project" = publications only; "global" = globally published knowledge, identical for every project.
Memory-backed sources only. Also expose unowned legacy records written before ownership existed. Off by default: legacy records are preserved on disk but never become shared knowledge implicitly.

Memory-backed sources only. Bounded automatic selection is on by default: pinned kinds always, records relevant to the current message, a few recent captures, and an explicit account of what was left out. Override fields of the policy here, or set `false` to inject the full formatted log.
Every Kingdom integration this Foundry is paired as, once per Kingdom + owner; Signets stay in private files.
Paired Kingdoms (by URL) that may not open this Foundry's viewer. A paired Kingdom may unless it is listed. Changed only on this machine (`POST /api/kingdom/viewer`), never through a Kingdom.
Whether the initial setup wizard has been completed.

Dev mode for this project alone, over this machine's `__devMode` (R-2026-11-25-05): `true` sends this project's Warden calls to this machine's `__chorus` host while the rest stay local, `false` keeps them local while dev mode is on elsewhere. Machine only: never in a repository.
Whether this project is enabled. Default: true.
`archived`: hidden from the viewer's project list until unarchived; its settings and threads are kept and it still runs. Absent: live, its runtime status (active or idle) derived from its threads.

This project's Wardens: each knows one topic of the project and reminds its threads what already exists and where it's written down. Merged over the `chorus` of the repository's Chorus working copy (`~/.chorus/projects/<owner>/<repo>/.foundry/project.json`, kept by the Chorus host from the region store), these settings winning. Wardens run only when `enabled` is true; absent, the project has no Wardens and topics present are reported as off. In a resolved project view this is normalized (`enabled` effective, `layers` absolute); see docs/usage-and-context.md, "Chorus".
Run this project's Wardens. Off by default.
The one topics folder the Wardens read (absolute or relative to the Chorus working copy; default `.foundry/regions`).
Several topics folders in order, a later layer's topic replacing an earlier one (e.g. template base, then this project).
The `consumed` trigger: Wardens are asked when a thread takes in a work item. Off by default.
Ask the Wardens when a thread takes in a work item (a ticket, spec or issue it read). Off by default.
Globs on a tool's name; a matching call's output is the work item. Default `DEFAULT_CONSUMED_TOOLS`.
Globs on a read file's path, relative to the project; the file is the work item. Default `DEFAULT_CONSUMED_PATHS`.
The work item is clipped to this many characters, with a marker. Default 12,000.

The reception charter (`CHORUS_RECEPTION`): how the main thread reads a Warden's reminder, held once as a standing layer. On with the Wardens (themselves opt-in); `false` leaves it out, e.g. for a baseline.

How the Wardens classify (classify/): their stages, at most three. Omitted, the two-layer chain: Haiku 5.5 low answers with its why inline and escalates each yes, without the why, to Sonnet 5.5 low on the same knowledge.md (Oracle finding 2026-11-01-l2-nowhy); with API-token decisions, one stage. The machine's list replaces the repository's whole.
Its stages, each `{ model?, effort?, doc?, outcomes?, reason?, task?, pointer?, escalate?, carryWhy?, deadline? }`.

After a region Warden's decision is journalled, ask its last answering stage "why did you answer that?" with the stage's own exchange resent inline (classify `FOLLOWUP_QUESTION`), unless that stage's own follow-up gave it: its own call at the lowest priority, never on a held spare, journalled and archived beside the one it explains, never delaying it. On unless `false` (Aron, 2026-11-18: it stays on for now).
How Herald topics would classify: the socket only. Heralds are not built; their topics do not run.
Its stages, each `{ model?, effort?, doc?, outcomes?, reason?, task?, pointer?, escalate?, carryWhy?, deadline? }`.
This project's agent conversations (docs/reference/CONVERSATIONS.md §4.6): floor mode, depth bound and conch, over the repository's `conversations`, each thread's own overrides last.
This project's schedules: each run a thread in the project. This machine's only, never committed.
Where main threads get their subscription: this machine's login (`local`, the default) or a Kingdom pool.
How this project's threads balance this machine's logins, per runtime; over the Foundry-wide `subscriptionPools`.
Required when `capacity` is `kingdom`.
Paired Kingdom id or API origin (`bun run kingdom status`).
The Kingdom Signet that grants this project its subscription pool (`subscription.use`).
The one Kingdom project this Foundry project links to (Aron, 2026-11-01); its pool chooses a Kingdom-capacity login.
